changelog: [When to Segment]: Loosened the noun-phrase+particle rule to license a boundary even when a plain matrix verb, instruction/decision verb, or postposed subject/topic marker is still pending — withholding candidacy now applies only when the pending predicate is a reporting/opinion verb. Added two new permissive rules: (1) mark a candidate after every item in a coordinated/listed set of alternatives even before the shared governing verb appears, and (2) mark a candidate after an adverbial converb clause (-아서/어서, -다가, -고) even before the main verb that fixes its sense appears. These directly increase the number of marked boundaries available to the budget-trimming step, addressing the critic's coverage focus.

[Never Segment]: Narrowed the over-broad prohibition that blocked any boundary dependent on 'a governing verb not yet appeared' or 'a postposed subject/topic marker not yet appeared' — this was suppressing coverage on nearly every SOV clause. The prohibition now applies only to clauses whose meaning is directly reversed/reinterpreted by a later reporting/opinion verb, or to mid-repetition of an idiomatic connective phrase; plain matrix/instruction verbs and postposed subjects no longer block candidacy, they simply rank low.
